text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- Government launches reform of DGA arms procurement agency with the aim of increasing competitiveness. Details restructuring of aircraft maker Aerospatiale into two units, an aeronautics and a defence and space unit.
-- Doctors' unions to negotiate the implementation of social security authorities' plans to make big savings in 1997 through tightened health costs.
-- Bourse watchdog COB opens an inquiry over the release of information to the press concerning talks between CGIP and Cerus .
-- Defence Minister Charles Millon calls for cost cutting and restructuring of defence industry. Naval shipyards could shed 2,000 jobs by 1998.
-- Government considers reform of minimal "RMI" allowance, introducing idea that families of unemployed people could help support them, if their own income allows for it.
-- Finance Minister Jean Arthuis sends to E.U. authorities new Credit Lyonnais bailout plan.
-- EDF Chairman and former Economy Minister Edmond Alphandery restructures electricity supplier's decision-making processes.
-- Group of Fifteen near agreement on monetary stability pact, issue of sanctions against a country failing to keep its public deficit under three percent of GDP could be settled soon.
-- Food group Saint Louis chairman Daniel Melin says group profits fell 44 percent in the first half partly due to poor performance of paper branch, needs restructuring.
-- Workers at CIC fear for their jobs. Bidders interested in the ailing bank's privatisation must make public their interest by October 7.
-- Renault auto branch lost 911 million francs for the first half, plans to shed jobs next year by speeding up a cost-cutting plan.
